tagline: Tasks, a Pomodoro timer, and a habit tracker bundled in one app
verdictSummary: A task list with due dates, basic recurrence, and a built-in Pomodoro timer and simple habit tracker — TickTick's actual bundle, beyond plain task management already covered by this catalogue's Todoist entry — is a genuine one-sitting build. What doesn't survive: cross-device real-time sync and calendar integration polish refined over years.
coreLoopDIY: Manage tasks with due dates and simple recurrence, run a Pomodoro-style focus timer linked to a selected task, and track daily habit completion in the same app.
whatYouLose: years of edge-case handling for recurring tasks
whyPeopleStillPay: A task list and a timer are simple; keeping them in perfect sync across every device you own, instantly, for years, is the infrastructure work underneath the bundle.
prompt: Build a task manager bundling three things TickTick actually combines, beyond plain task management: a task list with due dates and recurrence, a Pomodoro-style focus timer, and a simple daily habit tracker. Use a local-first approach — Tauri with SQLite, or a simple web app if cross-device use matters more than offline-first — since real-time multi-device sync is explicitly out of scope. Implement tasks with due dates, priority, and basic recurrence rules (daily, weekly, every N days). Build a Pomodoro timer that can be linked to a specific task — start a 25-minute focus session against a chosen task, and log completed sessions per task. Add a simple habit tracker: named habits with a daily check-off, and a streak counter. Show all three — today's tasks, an optional active timer, and today's habits — on one combined daily view, since that bundled view is the actual point, not three separate apps. Do not build real-time cross-device sync, calendar integration, or shared or collaborative task lists — those are out of scope; this is a single-device, single-user tool. Requires a local database; no external API key needed.

faq.q: Does it sync between my phone and computer?
faq.a: Not in this build — that's explicitly out of scope. Each device would run its own independent local copy, which is a real step down from TickTick's cross-device sync.

faq.q: Is the Pomodoro timer actually linked to specific tasks?
faq.a: Yes — sessions are tied to a chosen task, and completed sessions are logged per task, matching TickTick's own bundled approach rather than being a separate, disconnected timer app.

faq.q: Can I share a task list with someone else?
faq.a: No — this is a single-user, single-device tool with no collaboration feature.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Nothing beyond running it locally — there's no subscription, since it's a single-device tool with no backend to host.
